page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E2.1 is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for entry-level enterprise deployments and balanced computing needs. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7551 processor running on the x86_64 architecture with a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. Compute capacity is derived from 1 dedicated physical core executing 2 hardware threads, presenting 2 vCPUs to the guest operating system. Dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable compute delivery free from neighbor contention.

Memory provisioning stands at 8.0 GB total RAM, yielding an even 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio appropriate for standard multi-tier infrastructure. The VM.Standard.E2.1 does not include bundled local storage, meaning disk access depends on attached network block volumes. It also contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for direct ingress and egress routing.

Because the hardware configuration employs early-generation EPYC architecture at modest base frequencies without local NVMe scratch space, it is positioned toward steady-state execution over high-throughput compute. It offers a cost-efficient resource footprint for foundational workloads. Best-fit use cases include lightweight web serving, internal utility tooling, small containerized services, development and staging servers, and background automation tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E2.1 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute environments. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7551 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 1 dedicated physical core mapped across 2 vCPUs. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle local disk storage, necessitating external network block storage for stateful deployments, and it excludes discrete GPU acceleration. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated core assignment offering consistent execution without resource contention, VM.Standard.E2.1 provides cost-effective infrastructure for lightweight web servers, development environments, continuous integration tasks, microservices, and modest application hosting.
